1	"""Graph construction, the CSR representation, and selectable read backends.
2	
3	Nodes are strings. Edges carry a numeric weight (default 1.0). Iteration order is always sorted, so
4	every algorithm in this package is deterministic without depending on insertion order.
5	
6	The mutable adjacency dict stays the single write layer -- ``add_node``, ``add_edge`` and
7	``remove_edge`` keep exactly their old semantics (undirected mirroring, self-loops, last-write-wins
8	on duplicates). ``configure_storage`` adds an optional read layer that ``nodes``, ``neighbors``,
9	``edges``, ``degree`` and every algorithm consult instead:
10	
11	* ``csr``   -- compressed sparse row: an 8-byte offset per node boundary plus a flattened
12	               16-byte (node id, weight) neighbour list, both kept sorted by node name;
13	* ``dense`` -- an n*n presence byte plus an n*n float64 weight, 9 bytes per cell. The presence byte
14	               is what lets a zero-weight edge stay distinct from a pair that has no edge;
15	* ``auto``  -- the smaller of the two logical footprints, CSR winning ties and every empty graph.
16	
17	A revision counter invalidates the arrays: any mutation rebuilds lazily on the next query, so a
18	switched graph still supports ``add_node``/``add_edge``/``remove_edge`` and immediately reflects them.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import math
24	from array import array
25	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
26	
27	from .errors import ValidationError
28	
29	DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES = 536870912
30	STORAGE_CHOICES = ("adjacency", "csr", "dense", "auto")
31	
32	
33	def _validated_weight(weight: object) -> float:
34	    """Normalise an edge weight to float, or raise ValidationError.
35	
36	    ``bool`` is rejected even though it subclasses ``int``; strings and ``None`` are rejected even
37	    though ``float()`` would accept some of them; and NaN plus the two infinities are rejected
38	    because a single non-finite value poisons every distance, rank and JSON document it reaches.
39	    Negative finite values are legal -- Bellman-Ford needs them.
40	    """
41	    if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, (int, float)):
42	        raise ValidationError("edge weight must be a finite number", value=weight)
43	    value = float(weight)
44	    if not math.isfinite(value):
45	        raise ValidationError("edge weight must be finite")
46	    return value
47	
48	
49	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
50	class Edge:
51	    source: str
52	    target: str
53	    weight: float = 1.0
54	
55	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
56	        if not self.source or not self.target:
57	            raise ValidationError("edge endpoints must be non-empty", value=f"{self.source!r}->{self.target!r}")
58	        object.__setattr__(self, "weight", _validated_weight(self.weight))
59	
60	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
61	        return {"source": self.source, "target": self.target, "weight": float(self.weight)}
62	
63	
64	@dataclass(slots=True)
65	class Graph:
66	    directed: bool = False
67	    _adjacency: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
68	
69	    # Backend actually read on queries: "adjacency" (the default), "csr" or "dense". ``auto`` is
70	    # resolved at selection time, so this field always names the materialised backend.
71	    _storage: str = field(default="adjacency", init=False)
72	    # What the caller passed to configure_storage; "auto" is preserved here for the stats report.
73	    _storage_requested: str | None = field(default=None, init=False)
74	    # Bumped on every mutation; the arrays carry the revision they were built at and rebuild
75	    # lazily whenever it lags (a same-shape weight overwrite must invalidate too).
76	    _revision: int = field(default=0, init=False)
77	    _built_revision: int = field(default=-1, init=False)
78	    # CSR arrays.
79	    _csr_nodes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
80	    _csr_offsets: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("q"), init=False)
81	    _csr_columns: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("q"), init=False)
82	    _csr_weights: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("d"), init=False)
83	    # Dense arrays. _dense_present[row * n + col] distinguishes a stored edge (its weight may be 0)
84	    # from a pair with no edge at all.
85	    _dense_nodes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
86	    _dense_index: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
87	    _dense_present: bytearray = field(default_factory=bytearray, init=False)
88	    _dense_weights: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("d"), init=False)
89	
90	    # -- construction ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	    def add_node(self, node: str) -> None:
92	        if not node:
93	            raise ValidationError("node name must be non-empty")
94	        if node not in self._adjacency:
95	            self._adjacency[node] = {}
96	            self._revision += 1
97	
98	    def add_edge(self, source: str, target: str, weight: float = 1.0) -> None:
99	        # Validate before touching any state: a rejected weight must add neither endpoint, overwrite
100	        # no existing edge, and -- for an undirected graph -- never leave just one half behind.
101	        value = _validated_weight(weight)
102	        self.add_node(source)
103	        self.add_node(target)
104	        if self.directed:
105	            self._adjacency[source][target] = value
106	        else:
107	            self._adjacency[source][target] = value
108	            self._adjacency[target][source] = value
109	        # A write of adjacency -- new arc or last-write-wins overwrite -- invalidates the arrays.
110	        self._revision += 1
111	
112	    def remove_edge(self, source: str, target: str) -> bool:
113	        removed = False
114	        if source in self._adjacency and target in self._adjacency[source]:
115	            del self._adjacency[source][target]
116	            removed = True
117	        if not self.directed and target in self._adjacency and source in self._adjacency[target]:
118	            del self._adjacency[target][source]
119	            removed = True
120	        if removed:
121	            self._revision += 1
122	        return removed
123	
124	    @classmethod
125	    def from_edges(cls, edges: list[Edge], *, directed: bool = False) -> "Graph":
126	        graph = cls(directed=directed)
127	        for edge in edges:
128	            graph.add_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.weight)
129	        return graph
130	
131	    # -- storage selection -----------------------------------------------------------------------
132	    def storage_sizes(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
133	        """Logical footprints ``(adjacency_entries, csr_bytes, dense_bytes)``.
134	
135	        ``n`` is the node count and ``a`` the total number of adjacency entries across every node:
136	        each directed arc counts once, an undirected non-self-loop edge counts twice (reachable from
137	        both ends) and a self-loop once. CSR is ``8*(n+1) + 16*a`` bytes; dense is ``9*n*n``.
138	        """
139	        n = len(self._adjacency)
140	        entries = sum(len(neighbours) for neighbours in self._adjacency.values())
141	        csr_bytes = 8 * (n + 1) + 16 * entries
142	        dense_bytes = 9 * n * n
143	        return entries, csr_bytes, dense_bytes
144	
145	    def _build_csr(self) -> None:
146	        nodes = sorted(self._adjacency)
147	        index = {node: position for position, node in enumerate(nodes)}
148	        offsets = array("q", [0])
149	        columns = array("q")
150	        weights = array("d")
151	        for node in nodes:
152	            for target in sorted(self._adjacency[node]):
153	                columns.append(index[target])
154	                weights.append(self._adjacency[node][target])
155	            offsets.append(len(columns))
156	        self._csr_nodes, self._csr_offsets = nodes, offsets
157	        self._csr_columns, self._csr_weights = columns, weights
158	
159	    def _build_dense(self) -> None:
160	        nodes = sorted(self._adjacency)
161	        n = len(nodes)
162	        required = 9 * n * n
163	        # The limit holds for the lazy post-mutation rebuild too: a graph that grew past it must
164	        # never attempt the allocation on its next query.
165	        if required > DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES:
166	            raise ValidationError(
167	                "dense storage exceeds the allocation limit",
168	                requestedBytes=required,
169	                limitBytes=DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES,
170	            )
171	        index = {node: position for position, node in enumerate(nodes)}
172	        present = bytearray(n * n)
173	        weights = array("d", [0.0]) * (n * n)
174	        for source in nodes:
175	            row = index[source] * n
176	            for target, weight in self._adjacency[source].items():
177	                cell = row + index[target]
178	                present[cell] = 1
179	                weights[cell] = weight
180	        self._dense_nodes, self._dense_index = nodes, index
181	        self._dense_present, self._dense_weights = present, weights
182	
183	    def configure_storage(self, requested: str = "adjacency") -> dict[str, object]:
184	        """Select the backend used by every read, and return the stable stats ``storage`` document.
185	
186	        ``adjacency`` restores the mutable dict. ``csr`` and ``dense`` materialise their arrays now
187	        (and re-materialise lazily after any mutation). ``auto`` compares the logical footprints
188	        after a full load and keeps the smaller one -- CSR on a tie, and always CSR for an empty
189	        graph; an oversized dense candidate under ``auto`` also falls back to CSR. An explicit
190	        ``dense`` whose matrix would exceed ``DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES`` is refused before any allocation.
191	        """
192	        if requested not in STORAGE_CHOICES:
193	            raise ValidationError(
194	                f"storage must be one of {', '.join(STORAGE_CHOICES)}",
195	                value=requested,
196	            )
197	        entries, csr_bytes, dense_bytes = self.storage_sizes()
198	        n = len(self._adjacency)
199	        selected = requested
200	        if requested == "auto":
201	            selected = "csr" if n == 0 or csr_bytes <= dense_bytes else "dense"
202	            if selected == "dense" and dense_bytes > DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES:
203	                selected = "csr"
204	        if selected == "dense":
205	            if dense_bytes > DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES:
206	                raise ValidationError(
207	                    "dense storage exceeds the allocation limit",
208	                    requestedBytes=dense_bytes,
209	                    limitBytes=DENSE_LIMIT_BYTES,
210	                )
211	            self._build_dense()
212	        elif selected == "csr":
213	            self._build_csr()
214	        self._storage = selected
215	        self._storage_requested = requested
216	        self._built_revision = self._revision
217	        return self.storage_document()
218	
219	    def _ensure_storage(self) -> None:
220	        """Rebuild the active arrays if a mutation happened after they were built."""
221	        if self._built_revision == self._revision:
222	            return
223	        if self._storage == "csr":
224	            self._build_csr()
225	        elif self._storage == "dense":
226	            self._build_dense()
227	        self._built_revision = self._revision
228	
229	    def storage_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
230	        """The ``storage`` object stats emits: request, selection, footprints and density."""
231	        entries, csr_bytes, dense_bytes = self.storage_sizes()
232	        n = len(self._adjacency)
233	        density = round(entries / (n * n), 10) if n else 0
234	        # adjacency has no formula of its own: its logical footprint is the same adjacency entries
235	        # laid out as CSR, which is the encoding csr() already exports.
236	        logical_bytes = {"adjacency": csr_bytes, "csr": csr_bytes, "dense": dense_bytes}[self._storage]
237	        return {
238	            "requested": self._storage_requested or "adjacency",
239	            "selected": self._storage,
240	            "logicalBytes": logical_bytes,
241	            "csrBytes": csr_bytes,
242	            "denseBytes": dense_bytes,
243	            "adjacencyEntries": entries,
244	            "density": density,
245	        }
246	
247	    # -- queries ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
248	    @property
249	    def node_count(self) -> int:
250	        return len(self._adjacency)
251	
252	    def nodes(self) -> list[str]:
253	        if self._storage == "csr":
254	            self._ensure_storage()
255	            return list(self._csr_nodes)
256	        if self._storage == "dense":
257	            self._ensure_storage()
258	            return list(self._dense_nodes)
259	        return sorted(self._adjacency)
260	
261	    def neighbors(self, node: str) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
262	        if self._storage == "csr":
263	            self._ensure_storage()
264	            try:
265	                row = self._csr_nodes.index(node)
266	            except ValueError:
267	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown node: {node}", known=list(self._csr_nodes[:10])) from None
268	            start, end = self._csr_offsets[row], self._csr_offsets[row + 1]
269	            return [
270	                (self._csr_nodes[self._csr_columns[position]], self._csr_weights[position])
271	                for position in range(start, end)
272	            ]
273	        if self._storage == "dense":
274	            self._ensure_storage()
275	            if node not in self._dense_index:

2	
3	Every function is deterministic (sorted iteration), reports unreachable nodes explicitly rather than
4	inventing a distance, and raises a typed error with evidence when the input makes the answer
5	undefined -- a negative edge for Dijkstra, a negative cycle for Bellman-Ford, a cycle for a
6	topological sort.

22	def _check_source(graph: Graph, source: str) -> None:
23	    if source not in graph.nodes():
24	        raise ValidationError(f"unknown source: {source}", known=graph.nodes()[:10])

27	def bfs(graph: Graph, source: str) -> dict[str, int]:
28	    """Hop distances from `source`; unreachable nodes are absent (never faked as -1)."""
29	    _check_source(graph, source)
30	    seen = {source: 0}
31	    queue = [source]
32	    head = 0
33	    while head < len(queue):
34	        node = queue[head]
35	        head += 1
36	        for neighbour, _ in graph.neighbors(node):
37	            if neighbour not in seen:
38	                seen[neighbour] = seen[node] + 1
39	                queue.append(neighbour)
40	    return seen

43	def dfs(graph: Graph, source: str) -> list[str]:
44	    """Pre-order depth-first walk, neighbours visited in sorted order."""
45	    _check_source(graph, source)
46	    visited: list[str] = []
47	    seen: set[str] = set()
48	    stack = [source]
49	    while stack:
50	        node = stack.pop()
51	        if node in seen:
52	            continue
53	        seen.add(node)
54	        visited.append(node)
55	        stack.extend(neighbour for neighbour, _ in reversed(graph.neighbors(node)) if neighbour not in seen)
56	    return visited

59	def dijkstra(graph: Graph, source: str) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict[str, str | None]]:
60	    """Non-negative shortest paths; a negative edge is refused, not silently mis-answered.
61	
62	    The check walks every edge once, up front: discovering a negative weight halfway through the
63	    relaxation loop would mean returning a distance that is simply wrong.
64	    """
65	    _check_source(graph, source)
66	    for edge in graph.edges():
67	        if edge.weight < 0:
68	            raise NegativeWeightError(
69	                "dijkstra requires non-negative weights; use bellman_ford",
70	                edge=f"{edge.source}->{edge.target}",
71	                weight=edge.weight,
72	            )
73	    distance: dict[str, float] = {source: 0.0}
74	    previous: dict[str, str | None] = {source: None}
75	    remaining = set(graph.nodes())
76	    while remaining:
77	        current = None
78	        best = INFINITY
79	        for node in sorted(remaining):
80	            if node in distance and distance[node] < best:
81	                current, best = node, distance[node]
82	        if current is None:
83	            break
84	        remaining.discard(current)
85	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(current):
86	            candidate = distance[current] + weight
87	            if neighbour not in distance or candidate < distance[neighbour]:
88	                distance[neighbour] = candidate
89	                previous[neighbour] = current
90	    return distance, previous

93	def bellman_ford(graph: Graph, source: str) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict[str, str | None]]:
94	    """Shortest paths with negative weights; reports the offending cycle when one exists."""
95	    _check_source(graph, source)
96	    distance: dict[str, float] = {source: 0.0}
97	    previous: dict[str, str | None] = {source: None}
98	    nodes = graph.nodes()
99	    for _ in range(len(nodes) - 1):
100	        changed = False
101	        for node in nodes:
102	            if node not in distance:
103	                continue
104	            for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
105	                candidate = distance[node] + weight
106	                if neighbour not in distance or candidate < distance[neighbour]:
107	                    distance[neighbour] = candidate
108	                    previous[neighbour] = node
109	                    changed = True
110	        if not changed:
111	            break
112	    for node in nodes:
113	        if node not in distance:
114	            continue
115	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
116	            if neighbour not in distance or distance[node] + weight < distance[neighbour]:
117	                raise NegativeCycleError("negative cycle reachable from the source", at=f"{node}->{neighbour}")
118	    return distance, previous

121	def path_from(previous: dict[str, str | None], target: str) -> list[str]:
122	    """Reconstruct a path from a predecessor map; raises when the target is unreachable."""
123	    if target not in previous:
124	        raise ValidationError(f"unreachable target: {target}")
125	    path = [target]
126	    while previous[path[-1]] is not None:
127	        path.append(str(previous[path[-1]]))
128	    return list(reversed(path))

131	def _validated_heuristic(graph: Graph, target: str, heuristic: Mapping[str, float] | None) -> dict[str, float]:
132	    """Normalise the heuristic map, or raise ValidationError naming the first offending entry.
133	
134	    Nodes missing from the map estimate to 0. Every supplied value must be a finite, non-negative
135	    number naming a node of the graph; the target must estimate to exactly 0; and along every
136	    traversable direction the estimate must be consistent -- h(u) <= weight(u, v) + h(v) -- which is
137	    what guarantees the first time the target leaves the frontier its distance is final. All checks
138	    walk nodes and edges in sorted order, so the reported violation never depends on the mapping's
139	    key order.
140	    """
141	    estimates = {node: 0.0 for node in graph.nodes()}
142	    if not heuristic:
143	        return estimates
144	    known = set(graph.nodes())
145	    for node in sorted(heuristic):
146	        value = heuristic[node]
147	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value):
148	            raise ValidationError("heuristic values must be finite numbers", node=node)
149	        estimate = float(value)
150	        if estimate < 0:
151	            raise ValidationError("heuristic values must be non-negative", node=node, value=estimate)
152	        if node not in known:
153	            raise ValidationError(f"heuristic names an unknown node: {node}", known=graph.nodes()[:10])
154	        estimates[node] = estimate
155	    if estimates[target] != 0.0:
156	        raise ValidationError("heuristic for the target must be 0", target=target, value=estimates[target])
157	    # A small tolerance keeps float summation noise (0.1 + 0.2) from reading as a violation; a real
158	    # inconsistency exceeds it by construction.
159	    for node in graph.nodes():
160	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
161	            if estimates[node] > weight + estimates[neighbour] + 1e-9:
162	                raise ValidationError(
163	                    "heuristic is not consistent: h(u) must not exceed weight(u, v) + h(v)",
164	                    edge=f"{node}->{neighbour}",
165	                    estimate=estimates[node],
166	                    bound=round(weight + estimates[neighbour], 10),
167	                )
168	    return estimates

171	def astar(
172	    graph: Graph,
173	    source: str,
174	    target: str,
175	    heuristic: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
176	) -> tuple[float, dict[str, str | None], int]:
177	    """Goal-directed shortest path from `source` to `target` guided by a consistent heuristic.
178	
179	    Returns the distance to `target`, a predecessor map `path_from` can rebuild the route from, and
180	    the number of distinct nodes expanded. The frontier is a heap keyed by (estimated total cost,
181	    node name), so equal-cost candidates and equal-cost paths are always settled by node name; with
182	    an empty heuristic the search degenerates to Dijkstra and agrees with it exactly. A negative
183	    edge is refused up front, an unreachable target raises rather than inventing a distance.
184	    """
185	    _check_source(graph, source)
186	    if target not in graph.nodes():
187	        raise ValidationError(f"unknown target: {target}", known=graph.nodes()[:10])
188	    for edge in graph.edges():
189	        if edge.weight < 0:
190	            raise NegativeWeightError(
191	                "astar requires non-negative weights; use bellman_ford",
192	                edge=f"{edge.source}->{edge.target}",
193	                weight=edge.weight,
194	            )
195	    estimates = _validated_heuristic(graph, target, heuristic)
196	    distance: dict[str, float] = {source: 0.0}
197	    previous: dict[str, str | None] = {source: None}
198	    frontier: list[tuple[float, str]] = [(estimates[source], source)]
199	    expanded: set[str] = set()
200	    while frontier:
201	        _, current = heapq.heappop(frontier)
202	        if current in expanded:
203	            continue
204	        expanded.add(current)
205	        if current == target:
206	            return distance[target], previous, len(expanded)
207	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(current):
208	            if neighbour in expanded:
209	                continue
210	            candidate = distance[current] + weight
211	            if neighbour not in distance or candidate < distance[neighbour]:
212	                distance[neighbour] = candidate
213	                previous[neighbour] = current
214	                heapq.heappush(frontier, (candidate + estimates[neighbour], neighbour))
215	    raise ValidationError(f"unreachable target: {target}")

218	def components(graph: Graph) -> list[list[str]]:
219	    """Weakly connected components, each sorted, the list ordered by its smallest node."""
220	    undirected = graph if not graph.directed else _as_undirected(graph)
221	    seen: set[str] = set()
222	    groups: list[list[str]] = []
223	    for node in undirected.nodes():
224	        if node in seen:
225	            continue
226	        group = sorted(bfs(undirected, node))
227	        seen.update(group)
228	        groups.append(group)
229	    return groups

232	def _as_undirected(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
233	    mirror = Graph(directed=False)
234	    # Seed every node before mirroring the edges: a node with no incident arc -- added on its own via
235	    # add_node or orphaned by remove_edge -- cannot be recovered from the edge list, yet it must
236	    # survive the undirected reading as a singleton component.
237	    for node in graph.nodes():
238	        mirror.add_node(node)
239	    for edge in graph.edges():
240	        mirror.add_edge(edge.source, edge.target, edge.weight)
241	    return mirror

244	def topological_sort(graph: Graph) -> list[str]:
245	    """Kahn's algorithm; a cycle is reported with the nodes that could never be released."""
246	    if not graph.directed:
247	        raise ValidationError("topological sort requires a directed graph")
248	    in_degree = {node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()}
249	    for node in graph.nodes():
250	        for neighbour, _ in graph.neighbors(node):
251	            in_degree[neighbour] += 1
252	    ready = sorted(node for node, degree in in_degree.items() if degree == 0)
253	    order: list[str] = []
254	    while ready:
255	        node = ready.pop(0)
256	        order.append(node)
257	        for neighbour, _ in graph.neighbors(node):
258	            in_degree[neighbour] -= 1
259	            if in_degree[neighbour] == 0:
260	                ready.append(neighbour)
261	                ready.sort()
262	    if len(order) != graph.node_count:
263	        stuck = sorted(node for node, degree in in_degree.items() if degree > 0)
264	        raise CycleError("directed cycle prevents a topological order", cycle=stuck)
265	    return order

269	class PageRankResult:
270	    scores: dict[str, float]
271	    iterations: int
272	    converged: bool
273	
274	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
275	        return {"iterations": self.iterations, "converged": self.converged, "scores": {node: round(value, 10) for node, value in sorted(self.scores.items())}}

278	def pagerank(graph: Graph, *, damping: float = 0.85, tolerance: float = 1e-9, max_iterations: int = 200) -> PageRankResult:
279	    """Power iteration with explicit convergence reporting (never a silent iteration cap).
280	
281	    Edge weights are transition shares, so a negative one would yield negative scores, a zero
282	    outgoing-weight sum that divides through to nonsense, or a total that is not one. The whole
283	    graph participates in the redistribution -- an edge in an isolated component is not exempt -- so
284	    every edge is checked up front in the graph's stable edge order and a negative weight is refused
285	    with that edge as evidence; a zero total is fine, it simply marks a dangling node.
286	    """
287	    if not 0.0 < damping < 1.0:
288	        raise ValidationError("damping must be in (0, 1)", value=damping)
289	    for edge in graph.edges():
290	        if edge.weight < 0:
291	            raise NegativeWeightError(
292	                "pagerank requires non-negative edge weights",
293	                edge=f"{edge.source}->{edge.target}",
294	                weight=edge.weight,
295	            )
296	    nodes = graph.nodes()
297	    if not nodes:
298	        return PageRankResult({}, 0, True)
299	    total = len(nodes)
300	    scores = {node: 1.0 / total for node in nodes}
301	    outgoing = {node: sum(weight for _, weight in graph.neighbors(node)) for node in nodes}
302	    # Incoming edges are collected once, outside the iteration loop: rebuilding the neighbour mapping
303	    # inside it was both quadratic and wasteful (the first version of this function did exactly that).
304	    incoming_edges: dict[str, list[tuple[str, float]]] = {node: [] for node in nodes}
305	    for node in nodes:
306	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
307	            incoming_edges[neighbour].append((node, weight))
308	    converged = False
309	    iterations = 0
310	    for iterations in range(1, max_iterations + 1):
311	        dangling = sum(scores[node] for node in nodes if outgoing[node] == 0)
312	        updated: dict[str, float] = {}
313	        for node in nodes:
314	            incoming = 0.0
315	            for other, weight in incoming_edges[node]:
316	                if outgoing[other] > 0:
317	                    incoming += scores[other] * weight / outgoing[other]
318	            updated[node] = (1.0 - damping) / total + damping * (incoming + dangling / total)
319	        delta = sum(abs(updated[node] - scores[node]) for node in nodes)
320	        scores = updated
321	        if delta < tolerance:
322	            converged = True
323	            break
324	    return PageRankResult(scores, iterations, converged)

327	def degree_centrality(graph: Graph) -> dict[str, float]:
328	    """Degree normality: degree divided by the largest possible degree in an undirected reading."""
329	    total = graph.node_count
330	    if total <= 1:
331	        return {node: 0.0 for node in graph.nodes()}
332	    denominator = float(total - 1)
333	    return {node: round(graph.degree(node) / denominator, 10) for node in graph.nodes()}

337	class ClusteringResult:

339	    average: float
340	    transitivity: float

347	            "average": self.average,
348	            "transitivity": self.transitivity,

355	def clustering(graph: Graph) -> ClusteringResult:
356	    """Local clustering coefficients, their average, and the global transitivity.
357	
358	    Everything is measured on a simple undirected reading of the graph: an edge in either direction
359	    counts once, weights and duplicate adjacencies are ignored, and self-loops are neighbours of
360	    nobody. Every node -- including isolated ones -- is present in the result and counts towards the
361	    average. Each unordered triangle is counted once; a connected triple (wedge) is counted at its
362	    centre as a pair of distinct neighbours. All iteration is sorted, so the answer never depends on
363	    insertion order or set traversal.
364	    """
365	    # Built directly instead of via _as_undirected: that helper mirrors edges only, so an isolated
366	    # node in a directed graph would silently drop out of the average.
367	    adjacency: dict[str, set[str]] = {node: set() for node in graph.nodes()}
368	    for edge in graph.edges():
369	        if edge.source == edge.target:
370	            continue
371	        adjacency[edge.source].add(edge.target)
372	        adjacency[edge.target].add(edge.source)
373	    nodes = sorted(adjacency)
374	    coefficients: dict[str, float] = {}
375	    coefficient_sum = 0.0
376	    closed_pairs = 0
377	    wedges = 0
378	    for node in nodes:
379	        neighbours = sorted(adjacency[node])
380	        degree = len(neighbours)
381	        pairs = degree * (degree - 1) // 2
382	        if degree < 2:
383	            coefficients[node] = 0.0
384	            continue
385	        # A linked pair of neighbours closes one wedge at this node; each triangle contributes at all
386	        # three of its vertices, so the total is three times the triangle count.
387	        between = sum(1 for index, left in enumerate(neighbours) for right in neighbours[index + 1 :] if right in adjacency[left])
388	        value = between / pairs
389	        coefficients[node] = round(value, 10)
390	        coefficient_sum += value
391	        closed_pairs += between
392	        wedges += pairs
393	    triangles = closed_pairs // 3
394	    average = round(coefficient_sum / len(nodes), 10) if nodes else 0.0
395	    transitivity = round(3 * triangles / wedges, 10) if wedges else 0.0
396	    return ClusteringResult(coefficients, average, transitivity, triangles, wedges)

420	def label_propagation(graph: Graph, *, max_iterations: int = 100) -> CommunitiesResult:
421	    """Deterministic weighted label propagation over a simple undirected reading of the graph.
422	
423	    The reading ignores self-loops and sums arcs between the same pair: an undirected edge
424	    contributes its weight once in each direction, and mutual arcs of a directed graph add up. Every
425	    node starts labelled with its own name; each round walks nodes in name order and moves a node to
426	    the neighbouring label with the highest summed edge weight, keeping the current label when it
427	    ties for the best score and otherwise preferring the lexicographically smallest tied label. A
428	    round with no change is convergence; hitting `max_iterations` first is reported honestly as
429	    `converged=False` with the deterministic labelling reached so far. Communities are the groups
430	    sharing a final label, each sorted by node name, the list ordered by each group's smallest node,
431	    and every output label is normalised to that smallest member -- so isolated nodes stay singleton
432	    communities and the document is byte-identical however the edges were ordered. Weights must be
433	    non-negative: the first negative edge in the graph's stable edge order is refused with that edge
434	    as evidence.
435	    """
436	    if isinstance(max_iterations, bool) or not isinstance(max_iterations, int) or max_iterations < 1:
437	        raise ValidationError("max_iterations must be an integer >= 1", value=max_iterations)
438	    for edge in graph.edges():
439	        if edge.weight < 0:
440	            raise NegativeWeightError(
441	                "label propagation requires non-negative edge weights",
442	                edge=f"{edge.source}->{edge.target}",
443	                weight=edge.weight,
444	            )
445	    nodes = graph.nodes()
446	    if not nodes:
447	        return CommunitiesResult([], {}, 0, True)
448	    adjacency: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {node: {} for node in nodes}
449	    for edge in graph.edges():
450	        if edge.source == edge.target:
451	            continue
452	        adjacency[edge.source][edge.target] = adjacency[edge.source].get(edge.target, 0.0) + edge.weight
453	        adjacency[edge.target][edge.source] = adjacency[edge.target].get(edge.source, 0.0) + edge.weight
454	    labels = {node: node for node in nodes}
455	    converged = False
456	    iterations = 0
457	    for iterations in range(1, max_iterations + 1):
458	        changed = False
459	        for node in nodes:
460	            scores: dict[str, float] = {}
461	            for neighbour in sorted(adjacency[node]):
462	                label = labels[neighbour]
463	                scores[label] = scores.get(label, 0.0) + adjacency[node][neighbour]
464	            if not scores:
465	                continue
466	            best = max(scores.values())
467	            tied = {label for label, score in scores.items() if score == best}
468	            if labels[node] in tied:
469	                continue
470	            labels[node] = min(tied)
471	            changed = True
472	        if not changed:
473	            converged = True
474	            break
475	    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
476	    for node in nodes:
477	        groups.setdefault(labels[node], []).append(node)
478	    # Members were appended in sorted node order, and lexicographic list ordering is then exactly
479	    # "ordered by the smallest member", which is the required community order.
480	    communities = sorted(groups.values())
481	    normalised = {node: members[0] for members in communities for node in members}
482	    return CommunitiesResult(communities, normalised, iterations, converged)
483

1	"""Shortest-path consistency regression: three algorithms, two entry points, one answer.
2	
3	Every graph in the battery uses finite integer weights so an exact float comparison can never
4	mistake rounding noise for an algorithmic disagreement. For each non-negative graph and each
5	source, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford and A* (with an all-zero heuristic) must report the same reachable
6	set and the same distances -- through both the Python API and the CLI. Where several shortest
7	routes tie, the algorithms may pick different ones, but every returned route must start at the
8	source, end at the target, walk real traversable edges, and sum to the reported distance.
9

11	simple-path oracle; Dijkstra, A* and compare must keep refusing them with NegativeWeightError.

108	def traversable_weights(graph: Graph) -> dict[tuple[str, str], float]:
109	    """Every directed step the graph actually allows, with its weight."""
110	    return {(node, neighbour): weight for node in graph.nodes() for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node)}

113	def assert_real_path(
114	    case: unittest.TestCase,
115	    weights: dict[tuple[str, str], float],
116	    path: list[str],
117	    source: str,
118	    target: str,
119	    distance: float,
120	) -> None:
121	    """A returned route must walk real edges from source to target and sum to the distance."""
122	    case.assertEqual(path[0], source)
123	    case.assertEqual(path[-1], target)
124	    total = 0.0
125	    for step_source, step_target in zip(path, path[1:]):
126	        case.assertIn((step_source, step_target), weights)
127	        total += weights[(step_source, step_target)]
128	    case.assertEqual(total, distance)

131	def simple_path_distances(graph: Graph, source: str) -> dict[str, float]:
132	    """Independent oracle: the cheapest simple path to every node, by exhaustive enumeration.
133	
134	    With no reachable negative cycle a shortest walk never repeats a node, so the minimum over
135	    simple paths is the true shortest distance -- computed here without any relaxation machinery.
136	    """
137	    best = {source: 0.0}
138	
139	    def walk(node: str, cost: float, seen: frozenset[str]) -> None:
140	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
141	            if neighbour in seen:
142	                continue
143	            candidate = cost + weight
144	            if neighbour not in best or candidate < best[neighbour]:
145	                best[neighbour] = candidate
146	            walk(neighbour, candidate, seen | {neighbour})
147	
148	    walk(source, 0.0, frozenset({source}))
149	    return best

"""Shortest-path consistency regression: three algorithms, two entry points, one answer.

Every graph in the battery uses finite integer weights so an exact float comparison can never
mistake rounding noise for an algorithmic disagreement. For each non-negative graph and each
source, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford and A* (with an all-zero heuristic) must report the same reachable
set and the same distances -- through both the Python API and the CLI. Where several shortest
routes tie, the algorithms may pick different ones, but every returned route must start at the
source, end at the target, walk real traversable edges, and sum to the reported distance.

Negative weights are only exercised through Bellman-Ford, checked against an independent
simple-path oracle; Dijkstra, A* and compare must keep refusing them with NegativeWeightError.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
import unittest.mock

from graphtk import (
    Graph,
    NegativeCycleError,
    NegativeWeightError,
    ValidationError,
    astar,
    bellman_ford,
    dijkstra,
    path_from,
)
from graphtk.cli import EXIT_ERROR, EXIT_NEGATIVE, EXIT_OK, main


def run_cli(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
        code = main(argv)
    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()


# -- the graph battery ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One definition per graph -- name, directedness, JSONL-ready rows -- so the Python-level and the
# CLI-level tests exercise exactly the same graph, duplicate rows and all. Weights stay integral.
BATTERY: list[tuple[str, bool, list[tuple[str, str, int]]]] = [
    # Undirected, connected, with a tie: a->c costs 4 directly and 2 + 2 via b.
    (
        "undirected_connected",
        False,
        [("a", "b", 2), ("b", "c", 2), ("a", "c", 4), ("c", "d", 3), ("d", "e", 1), ("c", "e", 6)],
    ),
    # Directed and connected, with equal-length candidates: a reaches c for 2 both directly and
    # via b, and reaches d for 3 via b and via c.
    (
        "directed_connected",
        True,
        [("a", "b", 1), ("a", "c", 2), ("b", "c", 1), ("b", "d", 2), ("c", "d", 1), ("d", "e", 4), ("a", "e", 9)],
    ),
    # Two components plus a node only a self-loop touches: from any source, some nodes are
    # unreachable and must simply be absent from the distance map.
    (
        "disconnected_directed",
        True,
        [("a", "b", 3), ("c", "d", 2), ("e", "e", 4)],
    ),
    # Zero-weight edges: the cheapest route costs nothing at all for two hops.
    (
        "zero_weight_edges",
        True,
        [("a", "b", 0), ("b", "c", 0), ("a", "c", 5), ("c", "d", 1)],
    ),
    # Self-loops, one of them zero-weight: never part of a shortest route, never an error.
    (
        "self_loops",
        False,
        [("a", "a", 7), ("a", "b", 1), ("b", "b", 0), ("b", "c", 2)],
    ),
    # A repeated edge: the later row overwrites the earlier one, so a->b costs 2, not 9.
    (
        "duplicate_edges",
        True,
        [("a", "b", 9), ("a", "b", 2), ("b", "c", 1)],
    ),
    # From source a only a itself is reachable; the b<->c pair is a separate component.
    (
        "single_reachable_node",
        True,
        [("a", "a", 5), ("b", "c", 1), ("c", "b", 1)],
    ),
    # A square of unit edges: two equal shortest routes from a to d.
    (
        "equal_length_routes",
        False,
        [("a", "b", 1), ("b", "d", 1), ("a", "c", 1), ("c", "d", 1)],
    ),
]


def build_graph(directed: bool, rows: list[tuple[str, str, int]]) -> Graph:
    graph = Graph(directed=directed)
    for source, target, weight in rows:
        graph.add_edge(source, target, weight)
    return graph


def traversable_weights(graph: Graph) -> dict[tuple[str, str], float]:
    """Every directed step the graph actually allows, with its weight."""
    return {(node, neighbour): weight for node in graph.nodes() for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node)}


def assert_real_path(
    case: unittest.TestCase,
    weights: dict[tuple[str, str], float],
    path: list[str],
    source: str,
    target: str,
    distance: float,
) -> None:
    """A returned route must walk real edges from source to target and sum to the distance."""
    case.assertEqual(path[0], source)
    case.assertEqual(path[-1], target)
    total = 0.0
    for step_source, step_target in zip(path, path[1:]):
        case.assertIn((step_source, step_target), weights)
        total += weights[(step_source, step_target)]
    case.assertEqual(total, distance)


def simple_path_distances(graph: Graph, source: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Independent oracle: the cheapest simple path to every node, by exhaustive enumeration.

    With no reachable negative cycle a shortest walk never repeats a node, so the minimum over
    simple paths is the true shortest distance -- computed here without any relaxation machinery.
    """
    best = {source: 0.0}

    def walk(node: str, cost: float, seen: frozenset[str]) -> None:
        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node):
            if neighbour in seen:
                continue
            candidate = cost + weight
            if neighbour not in best or candidate < best[neighbour]:
                best[neighbour] = candidate
            walk(neighbour, candidate, seen | {neighbour})

    walk(source, 0.0, frozenset({source}))
    return best


# -- Python entry point ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CrossAlgorithmAgreementTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_distances_agree_across_all_three_algorithms(self) -> None:
        for name, directed, rows in BATTERY:
            graph = build_graph(directed, rows)
            for source in graph.nodes():
                with self.subTest(graph=name, source=source):
                    dijkstra_distance, _ = dijkstra(graph, source)
                    bellman_distance, _ = bellman_ford(graph, source)
                    self.assertEqual(sorted(dijkstra_distance), sorted(bellman_distance))
                    for node in dijkstra_distance:
                        self.assertEqual(dijkstra_distance[node], bellman_distance[node])
                    zero_heuristic = {node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()}
                    for target in dijkstra_distance:
                        distance, _, _ = astar(graph, source, target, zero_heuristic)
                        self.assertEqual(distance, dijkstra_distance[target])

    def test_every_returned_path_is_real_and_sums_to_the_distance(self) -> None:
        for name, directed, rows in BATTERY:
            graph = build_graph(directed, rows)
            weights = traversable_weights(graph)
            zero_heuristic = {node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()}
            for source in graph.nodes():
                dijkstra_distance, dijkstra_previous = dijkstra(graph, source)
                bellman_distance, bellman_previous = bellman_ford(graph, source)
                for target in dijkstra_distance:
                    with self.subTest(graph=name, source=source, target=target):
                        _, astar_previous, _ = astar(graph, source, target, zero_heuristic)
                        for previous in (dijkstra_previous, bellman_previous, astar_previous):
                            path = path_from(previous, target)
                            assert_real_path(self, weights, path, source, target, dijkstra_distance[target])
                        self.assertEqual(bellman_distance[target], dijkstra_distance[target])

    def test_duplicate_rows_keep_the_last_weight(self) -> None:
        graph = build_graph(True, [("a", "b", 9), ("a", "b", 2), ("b", "c", 1)])
        distance, _ = dijkstra(graph, "a")
        self.assertEqual(distance, {"a": 0.0, "b": 2.0, "c": 3.0})

    def test_single_reachable_node_reports_exactly_the_source(self) -> None:
        graph = build_graph(True, [("a", "a", 5), ("b", "c", 1), ("c", "b", 1)])
        for distances in (dijkstra(graph, "a")[0], bellman_ford(graph, "a")[0]):
            self.assertEqual(distances, {"a": 0.0})


class NegativeWeightTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Bellman-Ford alone handles negative edges; the others must keep refusing them."""

    def graph(self) -> Graph:
        # No negative cycle: from a, the distances are b=1, c=-1 (via b), d=0 (via b, c).
        return build_graph(
            True,
            [("a", "b", 1), ("a", "c", 4), ("b", "c", -2), ("c", "d", 1), ("b", "d", 5), ("e", "f", 3)],
        )

    def test_bellman_ford_matches_the_independent_oracle(self) -> None:
        graph = self.graph()
        distance, _ = bellman_ford(graph, "a")
        self.assertEqual(distance, simple_path_distances(graph, "a"))
        self.assertEqual(distance, {"a": 0.0, "b": 1.0, "c": -1.0, "d": 0.0})

    def test_reconstructed_paths_are_real_and_sum_to_the_distance(self) -> None:
        graph = self.graph()
        weights = traversable_weights(graph)
        distance, previous = bellman_ford(graph, "a")
        for target in distance:
            with self.subTest(target=target):
                assert_real_path(self, weights, path_from(previous, target), "a", target, distance[target])

    def test_dijkstra_and_astar_keep_refusing_negative_weights(self) -> None:
        graph = self.graph()
        with self.assertRaises(NegativeWeightError):
            dijkstra(graph, "a")
        with self.assertRaises(NegativeWeightError):
            astar(graph, "a", "d", {node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()})


class NegativeCycleTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def graph(self) -> Graph:
        # b -> c -> b totals -1, reachable from a.
        return build_graph(True, [("a", "b", 1), ("b", "c", -2), ("c", "b", 1)])

    def test_bellman_ford_raises_a_stable_negative_cycle_error(self) -> None:
        graph = self.graph()
        with self.assertRaises(NegativeCycleError) as first:
            bellman_ford(graph, "a")
        with self.assertRaises(NegativeCycleError) as second:
            bellman_ford(graph, "a")
        self.assertEqual(first.exception.to_document(), second.exception.to_document())


class ValidationFailureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unknown_source_is_a_validation_error_for_every_algorithm(self) -> None:
        graph = build_graph(False, [("a", "b", 1)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            dijkstra(graph, "missing")
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            bellman_ford(graph, "missing")
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            astar(graph, "missing", "a", None)

    def test_path_from_an_unreachable_target_is_a_validation_error(self) -> None:
        graph = build_graph(True, [("a", "b", 3), ("c", "d", 2)])
        _, previous = dijkstra(graph, "a")
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            path_from(previous, "c")

    def test_astar_with_an_unreachable_target_is_a_validation_error(self) -> None:
        graph = build_graph(True, [("a", "b", 3), ("c", "d", 2)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            astar(graph, "a", "c", {node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()})


# -- CLI entry point ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CompareCommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def write_edges(self, rows: list[tuple[str, str, int]], name: str = "edges.jsonl") -> str:
        path = os.path.join(self.directory.name, name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            for source, target, weight in rows:
                handle.write(json.dumps({"source": source, "target": target, "weight": weight}) + "\n")
        return path

    def write_heuristic(self, graph: Graph, name: str = "heuristic.json") -> str:
        path = os.path.join(self.directory.name, name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps({node: 0 for node in graph.nodes()}))
        return path

    def assert_error_document(self, out: str, err: str, kind: str) -> dict:
        """A failure: nothing on stdout, exactly one established-format JSON document on stderr."""
        self.assertEqual(out, "")
        lines = err.strip().splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 1)
        document = json.loads(lines[0])
        self.assertEqual(document["error"], kind)
        self.assertIn("message", document)
        return document

    def test_cli_distances_and_paths_agree_for_every_battery_graph(self) -> None:
        for name, directed, rows in BATTERY:
            graph = build_graph(directed, rows)
            weights = traversable_weights(graph)
            edges = self.write_edges(rows, f"{name}.jsonl")
            heuristic = self.write_heuristic(graph, f"{name}.heuristic.json")
            flag = ["--directed"] if directed else []
            for source in graph.nodes():
                with self.subTest(graph=name, source=source):
                    api_distance, _ = dijkstra(graph, source)
                    expected_code = EXIT_OK if len(api_distance) > 1 else EXIT_NEGATIVE

                    d_code, d_out, d_err = run_cli(["dijkstra", "--edges", edges, *flag, "--source", source])
                    b_code, b_out, b_err = run_cli(["bellman-ford", "--edges", edges, *flag, "--source", source])
                    self.assertEqual((d_code, d_err), (expected_code, ""))
                    self.assertEqual((b_code, b_err), (expected_code, ""))
                    dijkstra_doc = json.loads(d_out)
                    bellman_doc = json.loads(b_out)
                    # The CLI document is the API answer, rounded and with unreachable nodes omitted.
                    self.assertEqual(dijkstra_doc["distances"], {node: round(value, 10) for node, value in sorted(api_distance.items())})
                    self.assertEqual(dijkstra_doc["distances"], bellman_doc["distances"])
                    self.assertEqual(dijkstra_doc["reachable"], bellman_doc["reachable"])

                    for target in api_distance:
                        a_code, a_out, a_err = run_cli(
                            ["astar", "--edges", edges, *flag, "--source", source, "--target", target, "--heuristic", heuristic]
                        )
                        self.assertEqual((a_code, a_err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
                        astar_doc = json.loads(a_out)
                        self.assertEqual(astar_doc["distance"], round(api_distance[target], 10))
                        assert_real_path(self, weights, astar_doc["path"], source, target, api_distance[target])

                        t_code, t_out, t_err = run_cli(
                            ["dijkstra", "--edges", edges, *flag, "--source", source, "--target", target]
                        )
                        self.assertEqual((t_code, t_err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
                        target_doc = json.loads(t_out)
                        self.assertEqual(target_doc["distance"], round(api_distance[target], 10))
                        assert_real_path(self, weights, target_doc["path"], source, target, api_distance[target])

    def test_compare_reports_identical_with_reachable_and_compared_counts(self) -> None:
        rows = [("a", "b", 1), ("a", "c", 2), ("b", "c", 1), ("b", "d", 2), ("c", "d", 1), ("d", "e", 4), ("a", "e", 9)]
        edges = self.write_edges(rows)
        code, out, err = run_cli(["compare", "--edges", edges, "--directed", "--source", "a"])
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (EXIT_OK, ""))
        document = json.loads(out)
        self.assertTrue(document["identical"])
        self.assertEqual(document["nodesCompared"], 5)
        self.assertEqual(document["dijkstraReachable"], 5)
        self.assertEqual(document["bellmanFordReachable"], 5)
        self.assertNotIn("differences", document)

1	"""Reproducible state-sequence differential tests across the storage backends.
2	
3	The adjacency backend is the isomorphic reference graph and never leaves it. For each graph type
4	(directed and undirected) one reference graph and three peer graphs -- ``csr``, ``dense`` and
5	``auto``, configured to their named backend before the replay begins -- replay the *exact same*
6	sequence of ``add_node`` / ``add_edge`` / ``remove_edge`` / ``configure_storage`` operations. After
7	every successful step the peers must match the reference on the whole public observation surface
8	(nodes, edges, neighbours, degree, edge_count, self_loops, csr, to_document), on the storage sizes
9	and selection report (each interpreted for the backend currently selected), and -- whenever the
10	state's preconditions allow it -- on the complete results of every algorithm: BFS, DFS, Dijkstra,
11	Bellman-Ford, components, degree centrality, clustering, PageRank and label propagation. Directed
12	states additionally compare the topological sort (a cyclic state compares the raised CycleError
13	instead), reachable targets are compared through A* with the all-zero heuristic, and every
14	shortest-path ``path_from`` reconstruction is re-walked over edges that must still exist with weights
15	summing to the reported distance.
16	
17	The sequences come from a fixed linear congruential generator seeded with hard-coded values, so
18	repeated runs always choose the same cases and reach the same verdict -- no third-party random
19	testing library and no wall-clock input. Every failure message names the graph type, the backend,
20	the seed and the index of the first divergent step.
21	
22	The hand-written anchor sequences guarantee the required situations are actually visited in order:
23	isolated nodes, self-loops, zero-weight edges, duplicate-edge weight overwrites, removing a
24	non-existent edge (still ``False``), mutation after a backend switch, same-shape weight overwrites,
25	and consecutive switches between the materialised backends. Invalid operations (empty node names,
26	non-finite or non-numeric weights) must keep raising ``ValidationError`` on every backend with
27	identical evidence and leave no trace: nodes, edges, storage selection and subsequent algorithm
28	results are all unchanged.
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import unittest
34	from collections import Counter
35	
36	from graphtk import (
37	    Graph,
38	    CycleError,
39	    NegativeCycleError,
40	    NegativeWeightError,
41	    ValidationError,
42	    astar,
43	    bellman_ford,
44	    bfs,
45	    clustering,
46	    components,
47	    degree_centrality,
48	    dfs,
49	    dijkstra,
50	    label_propagation,
51	    path_from,
52	    pagerank,
53	    topological_sort,
54	)

56	PEERS = ("csr", "dense", "auto")
57	ALL_BACKENDS = ("adjacency", "csr", "dense", "auto")
58	
59	# Small finite weight universe: integers (exact in float64) plus the zero-weight case and a few
60	# dyadic fractions, so float sums compare exactly across summation orders. A legal negative value
61	# is included, so Dijkstra/A*/PageRank/label-propagation refusal paths occur as ordinary sequence
62	# steps; NaN/inf/strings/bool only appear as deliberately invalid operations.
63	WEIGHTS = [-3, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 0.5, 1.25, 2.5, 4.0]
64	INVALID_WEIGHTS = [float("nan"), float("inf"), float("-inf"), "2.0", None, True]
65	INVALID_NODE_NAMES = [""]  # add_node/add_edge reject exactly the empty string
66	
67	# Fixed LCG (Numerical Recipes constants), modulus 2**32: every "random" choice this module makes
68	# derives from it, so a given seed always reproduces the identical operation sequence.
69	LCG_MODULUS = 1 << 32
70	LCG_MULTIPLIER = 1664525
71	LCG_INCREMENT = 1013904223
72	
73	GENERATED_SEEDS = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
74	GENERATED_STEPS = 64
75	NODE_POOL = 6  # n <= 6 keeps dense far below the allocation limit and every algorithm cheap.
76

78	# -- deterministic sequence source ----------------------------------------------------------------
79	class SequenceRng:
80	    """The only source of choices: a seeded LCG with small bounded draws."""
81	
82	    def __init__(self, seed: int) -> None:
83	        self.state = seed & (LCG_MODULUS - 1)
84	
85	    def draw(self, bound: int) -> int:
86	        self.state = (LCG_MULTIPLIER * self.state + LCG_INCREMENT) % LCG_MODULUS
87	        return self.state % bound
88	
89	    def pick(self, values):
90	        return values[self.draw(len(values))]
91	
92	
93	# The anchor prefix makes the required special cases occur unconditionally, in a known order,
94	# before the generated churn begins: isolated node, self-loop, zero weight, duplicate overwrite
95	# (twice, including a same-shape overwrite back to the earlier weight), removal of an absent pair,
96	# a real deletion, then another self-loop and a re-add.
97	ANCHOR_PREFIX: tuple[tuple, ...] = (
98	    ("add_node", "iso"),                            # isolated node
99	    ("add_edge", "n0", "n0", 1.0),                 # self-loop
100	    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 0.0),                 # zero-weight edge
101	    ("add_edge", "n1", "n2", 2),                   # ordinary edge
102	    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 3),                   # duplicate edge: weight overwrite
103	    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 0.0),                 # same pair, overwrite back
104	    ("remove_edge", "n3", "n4"),                   # edge that never existed -> False
105	    ("remove_edge", "n1", "n2"),                   # real deletion (mirror half if undirected)
106	    ("add_edge", "n2", "n2", 5),                   # second self-loop
107	    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 1),                   # re-add after the churn
108	)
109	
110	# Hand-written tails: explicit post-switch mutation and consecutive materialised switches.
111	ANCHOR_TAILS: dict[str, list[tuple]] = {
112	    "switch_then_mutate": [
113	        ("configure", "csr"),
114	        ("add_node", "fresh"),
115	        ("add_edge", "n0", "fresh", 4),
116	        ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 7),                # overwrite while on csr
117	        ("remove_edge", "n0", "fresh"),
118	        ("configure", "dense"),
119	        ("add_edge", "fresh", "n2", 2),             # mutate while on dense
120	        ("remove_edge", "n2", "n2"),                # drop the self-loop
121	        ("configure", "adjacency"),
122	        ("add_edge", "iso", "n2", 1),               # mutate back on adjacency
123	    ],
124	    "consecutive_materialised_switches": [
125	        ("configure", "dense"),
126	        ("configure", "csr"),
127	        ("configure", "dense"),                     # dense -> csr -> dense, nothing in between
128	        ("configure", "auto"),
129	        ("add_edge", "n1", "n3", 0),                # zero-weight after repeated switches
130	        ("configure", "csr"),
131	        ("add_edge", "n3", "n3", 9),                # self-loop after repeated switches
132	        ("configure", "dense"),
133	        ("remove_edge", "n1", "n3"),
134	        ("configure", "auto"),
135	        ("configure", "adjacency"),
136	    ],

140	def generated_sequence(seed: int) -> list[tuple]:
141	    """Build one reproducible operation list from a fixed seed.
142	
143	    The mix is weighted toward edges and removals so the graph churns (overwrites, deletions of
144	    present and absent pairs, orphaned nodes) while staying tiny. A storage switch lands roughly
145	    every eighth step, cycling through every selection including adjacency. The anchor prefix is
146	    prepended and two materialised switches appended, so every generated run shares the required
147	    shapes and ends on the switched read paths.
148	    """
149	    rng = SequenceRng(seed)
150	    operations: list[tuple] = []
151	    for step in range(GENERATED_STEPS):
152	        kind = rng.draw(16)
153	        if step % 8 == 3:
154	            operations.append(("configure", rng.pick(ALL_BACKENDS)))
155	        elif kind < 2:
156	            operations.append(("add_node", f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}"))
157	        elif kind < 12:
158	            operations.append(
159	                (
160	                    "add_edge",
161	                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
162	                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
163	                    rng.pick(WEIGHTS),
164	                )
165	            )
166	        else:
167	            operations.append(
168	                (
169	                    "remove_edge",
170	                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
171	                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
172	                )
173	            )
174	    return [*ANCHOR_PREFIX, *operations, ("configure", "dense"), ("configure", "csr")]

178	def edge_rows(graph: Graph) -> list[tuple]:
179	    return [(edge.source, edge.target, edge.weight) for edge in graph.edges()]
180

182	def read_snapshot(graph: Graph) -> dict:
183	    """The public read surface that must be identical on every backend in the same state."""
184	    nodes = graph.nodes()
185	    return {
186	        "nodes": nodes,
187	        "edges": edge_rows(graph),
188	        "neighbors": {node: graph.neighbors(node) for node in nodes},
189	        "degrees": {node: graph.degree(node) for node in nodes},
190	        "edgeCount": graph.edge_count(),
191	        "selfLoops": graph.self_loops(),
192	        "csr": graph.csr(),
193	        "toDocument": graph.to_document(),
194	    }

197	def traversable_weights(graph: Graph) -> dict[tuple[str, str], float]:
198	    return {
199	        (node, neighbour): weight
200	        for node in graph.nodes()
201	        for neighbour, weight in graph.neighbors(node)
202	    }

205	def shortest_path_results(graph: Graph) -> dict:
206	    """BFS/DFS/Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford/A* for every source (and every reachable target).
207	
208	    Raises are part of the result: with a negative edge Dijkstra and A* refuse with
209	    NegativeWeightError while Bellman-Ford answers; a reachable negative cycle makes Bellman-Ford
210	    raise NegativeCycleError. The refusal documents are captured, so peers agree on exception type
211	    and evidence, not just on the successful answers. A* always runs in the non-negative case with
212	    the all-zero heuristic; its refusal document (same evidence for any target, since the edge scan
213	    happens first) is captured once per source in the negative case.
214	    """
215	    nodes = graph.nodes()
216	    zero_heuristic = {node: 0 for node in nodes}
217	    results: dict = {"sources": {}}
218	    for source in nodes:
219	        entry: dict = {"bfs": bfs(graph, source), "dfs": dfs(graph, source)}
220	        try:
221	            distance, previous = dijkstra(graph, source)
222	            entry["dijkstra"] = ("ok", distance, previous)
223	        except NegativeWeightError as error:
224	            entry["dijkstra"] = ("negative_weight", error.to_document())
225	
226	        try:
227	            distance, previous = bellman_ford(graph, source)
228	            entry["bellman"] = ("ok", distance, previous)
229	        except NegativeCycleError as error:
230	            entry["bellman"] = ("negative_cycle", error.to_document())
231	
232	        if entry["dijkstra"][0] == "ok":
233	            targets: dict[str, tuple] = {}
234	            for target in entry["dijkstra"][1]:
235	                targets[target] = astar(graph, source, target, zero_heuristic)
236	            entry["astar"] = ("ok", targets)
237	        else:
238	            # The up-front negative-edge scan refuses before the target is even consulted, so the
239	            # captured evidence is independent of which target was named.
240	            try:
241	                astar(graph, source, nodes[-1], zero_heuristic)
242	            except NegativeWeightError as error:
243	                entry["astar"] = ("negative_weight", error.to_document())
244	            else:  # pragma: no cover - a negative edge makes this branch unreachable
245	                raise AssertionError("astar accepted a graph carrying a negative edge")
246	        results["sources"][source] = entry
247	    return results

252	    results: dict = {

263	    except NegativeWeightError as error:

268	        except CycleError as error:

270	    else:

272	        try:
273	            topological_sort(graph)

276	        else:  # pragma: no cover - the production contract forbids this branch

334	class DifferentialHarness:
335	    def __init__(self, case: unittest.TestCase, directed: bool, seed: object) -> None:
336	        self.case = case

338	        self.seed = seed
339	        self.graph_type = "directed" if directed else "undirected"
340	        self.reference = Graph(directed=directed)
341	        self.peers = {name: Graph(directed=directed) for name in PEERS}
342	        # Peers start already switched, so the anchor prefix exercises lazy rebuilds on each

352	            f"first mismatch at step {step} ({what})"

356	        """The storage stats document a graph in the reference's state must report."""
357	        entries, csr_bytes, dense_bytes = self.reference.storage_sizes()
358	        n = self.reference.node_count
359	        density = round(entries / (n * n), 10) if n else 0
360	        logical_bytes = dense_bytes if selected == "dense" else csr_bytes
361	        return {

364	            "logicalBytes": logical_bytes,

"""Reproducible state-sequence differential tests across the storage backends.

The adjacency backend is the isomorphic reference graph and never leaves it. For each graph type
(directed and undirected) one reference graph and three peer graphs -- ``csr``, ``dense`` and
``auto``, configured to their named backend before the replay begins -- replay the *exact same*
sequence of ``add_node`` / ``add_edge`` / ``remove_edge`` / ``configure_storage`` operations. After
every successful step the peers must match the reference on the whole public observation surface
(nodes, edges, neighbours, degree, edge_count, self_loops, csr, to_document), on the storage sizes
and selection report (each interpreted for the backend currently selected), and -- whenever the
state's preconditions allow it -- on the complete results of every algorithm: BFS, DFS, Dijkstra,
Bellman-Ford, components, degree centrality, clustering, PageRank and label propagation. Directed
states additionally compare the topological sort (a cyclic state compares the raised CycleError
instead), reachable targets are compared through A* with the all-zero heuristic, and every
shortest-path ``path_from`` reconstruction is re-walked over edges that must still exist with weights
summing to the reported distance.

The sequences come from a fixed linear congruential generator seeded with hard-coded values, so
repeated runs always choose the same cases and reach the same verdict -- no third-party random
testing library and no wall-clock input. Every failure message names the graph type, the backend,
the seed and the index of the first divergent step.

The hand-written anchor sequences guarantee the required situations are actually visited in order:
isolated nodes, self-loops, zero-weight edges, duplicate-edge weight overwrites, removing a
non-existent edge (still ``False``), mutation after a backend switch, same-shape weight overwrites,
and consecutive switches between the materialised backends. Invalid operations (empty node names,
non-finite or non-numeric weights) must keep raising ``ValidationError`` on every backend with
identical evidence and leave no trace: nodes, edges, storage selection and subsequent algorithm
results are all unchanged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest
from collections import Counter

from graphtk import (
    Graph,
    CycleError,
    NegativeCycleError,
    NegativeWeightError,
    ValidationError,
    astar,
    bellman_ford,
    bfs,
    clustering,
    components,
    degree_centrality,
    dfs,
    dijkstra,
    label_propagation,
    path_from,
    pagerank,
    topological_sort,
)

PEERS = ("csr", "dense", "auto")
ALL_BACKENDS = ("adjacency", "csr", "dense", "auto")

# Small finite weight universe: integers (exact in float64) plus the zero-weight case and a few
# dyadic fractions, so float sums compare exactly across summation orders. A legal negative value
# is included, so Dijkstra/A*/PageRank/label-propagation refusal paths occur as ordinary sequence
# steps; NaN/inf/strings/bool only appear as deliberately invalid operations.
WEIGHTS = [-3, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 0.5, 1.25, 2.5, 4.0]
INVALID_WEIGHTS = [float("nan"), float("inf"), float("-inf"), "2.0", None, True]
INVALID_NODE_NAMES = [""]  # add_node/add_edge reject exactly the empty string

# Fixed LCG (Numerical Recipes constants), modulus 2**32: every "random" choice this module makes
# derives from it, so a given seed always reproduces the identical operation sequence.
LCG_MODULUS = 1 << 32
LCG_MULTIPLIER = 1664525
LCG_INCREMENT = 1013904223

GENERATED_SEEDS = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
GENERATED_STEPS = 64
NODE_POOL = 6  # n <= 6 keeps dense far below the allocation limit and every algorithm cheap.


# -- deterministic sequence source ----------------------------------------------------------------
class SequenceRng:
    """The only source of choices: a seeded LCG with small bounded draws."""

    def __init__(self, seed: int) -> None:
        self.state = seed & (LCG_MODULUS - 1)

    def draw(self, bound: int) -> int:
        self.state = (LCG_MULTIPLIER * self.state + LCG_INCREMENT) % LCG_MODULUS
        return self.state % bound

    def pick(self, values):
        return values[self.draw(len(values))]


# The anchor prefix makes the required special cases occur unconditionally, in a known order,
# before the generated churn begins: isolated node, self-loop, zero weight, duplicate overwrite
# (twice, including a same-shape overwrite back to the earlier weight), removal of an absent pair,
# a real deletion, then another self-loop and a re-add.
ANCHOR_PREFIX: tuple[tuple, ...] = (
    ("add_node", "iso"),                            # isolated node
    ("add_edge", "n0", "n0", 1.0),                 # self-loop
    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 0.0),                 # zero-weight edge
    ("add_edge", "n1", "n2", 2),                   # ordinary edge
    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 3),                   # duplicate edge: weight overwrite
    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 0.0),                 # same pair, overwrite back
    ("remove_edge", "n3", "n4"),                   # edge that never existed -> False
    ("remove_edge", "n1", "n2"),                   # real deletion (mirror half if undirected)
    ("add_edge", "n2", "n2", 5),                   # second self-loop
    ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 1),                   # re-add after the churn
)

# Hand-written tails: explicit post-switch mutation and consecutive materialised switches.
ANCHOR_TAILS: dict[str, list[tuple]] = {
    "switch_then_mutate": [
        ("configure", "csr"),
        ("add_node", "fresh"),
        ("add_edge", "n0", "fresh", 4),
        ("add_edge", "n0", "n1", 7),                # overwrite while on csr
        ("remove_edge", "n0", "fresh"),
        ("configure", "dense"),
        ("add_edge", "fresh", "n2", 2),             # mutate while on dense
        ("remove_edge", "n2", "n2"),                # drop the self-loop
        ("configure", "adjacency"),
        ("add_edge", "iso", "n2", 1),               # mutate back on adjacency
    ],
    "consecutive_materialised_switches": [
        ("configure", "dense"),
        ("configure", "csr"),
        ("configure", "dense"),                     # dense -> csr -> dense, nothing in between
        ("configure", "auto"),
        ("add_edge", "n1", "n3", 0),                # zero-weight after repeated switches
        ("configure", "csr"),
        ("add_edge", "n3", "n3", 9),                # self-loop after repeated switches
        ("configure", "dense"),
        ("remove_edge", "n1", "n3"),
        ("configure", "auto"),
        ("configure", "adjacency"),
    ],
}


def generated_sequence(seed: int) -> list[tuple]:
    """Build one reproducible operation list from a fixed seed.

    The mix is weighted toward edges and removals so the graph churns (overwrites, deletions of
    present and absent pairs, orphaned nodes) while staying tiny. A storage switch lands roughly
    every eighth step, cycling through every selection including adjacency. The anchor prefix is
    prepended and two materialised switches appended, so every generated run shares the required
    shapes and ends on the switched read paths.
    """
    rng = SequenceRng(seed)
    operations: list[tuple] = []
    for step in range(GENERATED_STEPS):
        kind = rng.draw(16)
        if step % 8 == 3:
            operations.append(("configure", rng.pick(ALL_BACKENDS)))
        elif kind < 2:
            operations.append(("add_node", f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}"))
        elif kind < 12:
            operations.append(
                (
                    "add_edge",
                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
                    f"n{rng.draw(NODE_POOL)}",
